account.history: Scanned from Wiegel's Erika model 33, made in Dresden in 1967, after fitting a new ribbon; Dresden's ribbon maker Barock closed in 2011.
account.use: OpenType rotates nine variants of each letter, numeral and main punctuation mark (supported e.g. by LibreOffice 5.3); includes ©, ®, typographic quotes, capital ß and pan-European accents.
account.notes: Roughest of the Erika trio; Erikas Büro is the cleaner sibling.

fonts.name: Erikas Büro
fonts.origin: Wiegel's own Erika typewriter
fonts.summary: A typewriter simulation in which every glyph exists in nine slightly different variants that OpenType cycles through, mimicking ribbon texture and uneven strikes. Extra stylistic sets handle chemical formulas, typographic quotes, superscripts and similar typewriter quirks.

account.what: A highly realistic typewriter font in Wiegel's Erika family.
account.history: Derived from his Erika typewriter fonts.
account.use: Each glyph exists in nine variants rotated by OpenType so repeated letters differ, with the first word's length setting the start point. Optional features: salt for chemical formulas, ss01 typographic quotes, ss02 ß to SS, ss03 superscript ²/³, ss04 o for zero, ss05 TeX logo, sups superscript digits. Needs OpenType software such as LibreOffice 5.3+; elsewhere it works without these effects.

fonts.name: Erika Type

account.history: Drawn from the type of Wiegel's own Erika typewriter, unlike its sibling Erika Ormig, which was scanned directly from ribbon impressions.

account.notes: The rounded stroke ends Wiegel copied turned out to be wear from cleaning.

account.what: An Art Nouveau jobbing typeface.
account.history: Benjamin Krebs added a type foundry to his Frankfurt bookshop in 1816; in 1857 it passed to Gustav Rosalino and type designer Hermann Poppelbaum, who issued Eureka around 1905. Wiegel digitised it in 2010.
account.use: Small-caps design, TrueType and webfont kit; some symbols had to be invented.
account.notes: Wiegel asks for original prints of the missing symbols and suggests the font for silent-film-style intertitles in family videos.

fonts.name: Europa Mittelschrift

account.what: A playful DIN 1451-style sans covering European scripts.
account.history: Inspired by Greek road signs using DIN-derived lettering; deliberately not bound to the norm.
account.use: Latin, extended Greek and Cyrillic, capital ß, UNZ1 and OpenType extras.

fonts.name: EuroScript

account.what: A joined school script covering Latin, Cyrillic and Greek.
account.history: A reworked, extended version of Wiegel's Lateinische Ausgangsschrift; Cyrillic checked with Russian teachers, Greek experimental because Greece has no official joined model.
account.use: Requires OpenType support (e.g. LibreOffice 5.3+); unusable otherwise. Cyrillic should suit Russian, Belarusian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian and Serbian-Macedonian.
account.notes: Some forms deviate from school norms, e.g. a 3 changed to avoid confusion with a Cyrillic letter. Wiegel asks users to direct complaints to software vendors.

fonts.name: Eyechart

account.what: Bold capitals from vision-test charts, extended into a full font.
account.history: Letters and numerals taken from eye-test charts; Wiegel, a glasses wearer since age five, knows them well.
account.use: Full accented capitals and punctuation; lowercase a–d hold Snellen hooks and e–l Landolt rings for building real eye charts or apps.

account.what: A semibold connected advertising script with a brush-pen feel.
account.history: Revival of 'Werbeschrift Mammut', a metal script released in 1932 by the Ludwig Wagner foundry in Leipzig, found in the fourth supplement of the Seemann type handbook; an existing digital version looked too unlike the original.

account.what: An OpenType upgrade of the Mammut connected advertising script.
account.history: Expands Wiegel's earlier digitisation of the 1932 Ludwig Wagner Mammut.
account.use: TrueType with calt and liga features: each capital exists solo and with joining stroke, each lowercase in four positional forms (isolated, initial, medial, final). Needs OpenType-aware software.
account.notes: The web page includes an editable sample text to try the font.

account.history: Second of his digitisations from 1950s Bauer foundry (Bauersche Gießerei) specimen cards; he chose the plainer alternate capitals over the ornate ones rivals used, giving a sterner look.

account.what: A loose, casual brush script.
account.history: Designed by Peter Schneidler in 1956 and cast by the Bauer foundry in Frankfurt; digitised from a Bauer specimen card, right after Manuskript Gothisch.

account.history: The Egyptian genre arose in England as eye-catching advertising type: Vincent Figgins issued the first in 1815 and a Thorne catalogue listed one in 1820; the 1930s brought geometric versions such as Memphis, the model here.
